+To read a historical file through Payload's file endpoint, include `?version=<version-id>`. Version reads generate these URLs for the main file, original, variants, and thumbnail. The requested filename and storage prefix must belong to that version, and both parent-document read access and version read access are enforced. Without `version`, the endpoint resolves current published files and the latest draft, subject to collection read access; filenames found only in history return 404.

+Stored historical files and originals serve their saved bytes without rerunning transformations, including when the URL contains resize parameters. A file built at request time instead goes through the same transformer pipeline as the current file. It uses that version's retained original and saved `_transforms`, not the current document's source or edits. Request parameters such as `?width=` apply to it as they do to the current file, and they need transform access in addition to read access. Without request parameters, a historical request is an ordinary read. Reading a historical file never saves new files or changes the version.

+A request-time historical file needs a compatible transformer. A request-time size also needs its name registered in the current configuration. If either is unavailable, the request fails instead of serving the current file or an untransformed original. Stored historical sizes remain readable even if their names are no longer configured. Public URLs supplied directly by a storage provider remain direct.

+Restoring a version preserves its saved content and file bytes, and saves the restored state as a new version. Storage references and URLs can change when Payload archives an outgoing file. Stored-only versions reuse their saved output bytes.

+A restore never builds new stored files. When the selected version includes a file built at request time, Payload handles each file on its own. A stored file keeps its saved bytes. A file built at request time stays request-time, built from the version's retained original and saved `_transforms`. Current size configuration determines the restored variants. Output bytes can differ when transformer code or configuration has changed.

+If the current configuration cannot build a request-time file, the restore fails with a 400 error before any file changes. If saving fails, Payload cleans up staged files through the existing file-operation lifecycle. Without database transactions, a failure after the document is written can leave the restored document saved; cleanup keeps files that it still references. Pass `draft: true` when restoring to create a draft without replacing the published document.

+Historical requests (`?version=<version-id>`) build request-time files from the selected version's original and saved `_transforms`. The handler receives that version's document snapshot, and the current compatible pipeline runs both phases, as for the current file: phase 1 applies the saved state, and phase 2 applies the request parameters. Stored historical files and originals continue to serve saved bytes without transformations. Restoring a version keeps its request-time entries request-time and its stored entries stored; a restore never builds new stored files. See [Historical file URLs](./overview#historical-file-urls) and [Restoring files](./overview#restoring-files).
